text: The area of the region, inside the circle $(x-2\sqrt{3})^{2}+y^{2}=12$ and outside the parabola $y^{2}=2\sqrt{3}x$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} \text{Required area}=2\int\limits _{0}^{2\sqrt{3}}\left (\sqrt{4\sqrt{3}x-x^{2}}-\sqrt{2\sqrt{3}x}\right )dx \\  \\ =2\int\limits _{0}^{2\sqrt{3}}\left (\sqrt{12-(x-2\sqrt{3})^{2}}-\sqrt{2\sqrt{3}x}\right )dx \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} =2\left [\frac{x-2\sqrt{3}}{2}\sqrt{12-(x-2\sqrt{3})^{2}}+\frac{12}{2}\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{x-2\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{3}}\right )-\frac{\sqrt{2\sqrt{3}}x^{\dfrac{3}{2}}}{\frac{3}{2}}\right ]_{0}^{2\sqrt{3}} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} =2\{3π-8\} \\  \\ =6π-16\text{sq. units.} \end{array}$

text: Let the foci of a hyperbola be $(1,14)$ and $(1,-12)$. If it passes through the point $(1,6)$, then the length of its latus-rectum is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The foci $S_{1}(1,14)$ and $S_{2}(1,-12)$ lie on the line $x=1$, so the transverse axis is along $x=1$, the centre is the mid-point $(1,1)$, and $2c=S_{1}S_{2}=26$, so $c=13$.


[IMG]

Take the hyperbola as $\dfrac{(y-1)^{2}}{a^{2}}-\dfrac{(x-1)^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$. Every point $P$ on it satisfies $|PS_{1}-PS_{2}|=2a$. For $P(1,6)$: $PS_{1}=8$ and $PS_{2}=18$, so $2a=10$ and $a=5$.

$b^{2}=c^{2}-a^{2}=169-25=144$

$\text{Length of latus rectum}=\frac{2b^{2}}{a}=\frac{2\times 144}{5}=\frac{288}{5}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: Let $z_{1},z_{2}$ and $z_{3}$ be three complex numbers on the circle $|z|=1$ with $\arg (z_{1})=\frac{-π}{4},\arg (z_{2})=0$ and $\arg (z_{3})=\frac{π}{4}$. If $|z_{1}\bar{z}_{2}+z_{2}\bar{z}_{3}+z_{3}\bar{z}_{1}|^{2}=α+β\sqrt{2},α,β\in Z$, then the value of $α^{2}+β^{2}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To solve the problem, we start with the given information about the complex numbers $z_{1},z_{2},$ and $z_{3}$, which lie on the unit circle $|z|=1$. Their arguments are as follows:

$\arg (z_{1})=-\frac{π}{4}$

$\arg (z_{2})=0$

$\arg (z_{3})=\frac{π}{4}$

Thus, the complex numbers can be represented as:

$z_{1}=e^{-i\frac{π}{4}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}$

$z_{2}=e^{i\cdot 0}=1$

$z_{3}=e^{i\frac{π}{4}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}$

Next, calculate the conjugates needed:

$\bar{z}_{2}=1$

$\bar{z}_{3}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\bar{z}_{1}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}$

We need to evaluate:

$z_{1}\bar{z}_{2}+z_{2}\bar{z}_{3}+z_{3}\bar{z}_{1}$

Calculate each term separately:

$z_{1}\bar{z}_{2}=\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right )\cdot 1=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}$

$z_{2}\bar{z}_{3}=1\cdot \left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right )=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}$

$z_{3}\bar{z}_{1}=\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right )\cdot \left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right )=\frac{(1+i)^{2}}{2}=\frac{1+2i-1}{2}=i$

Sum the evaluated terms:

$z_{1}\bar{z}_{2}+z_{2}\bar{z}_{3}+z_{3}\bar{z}_{1}=\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right )+\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{i}{\sqrt{2}}\right )+i$

Simplify: 

$=\sqrt{2}+i-\sqrt{2}i=\sqrt{2}+i(1-\sqrt{2})$

Calculate the modulus squared:

$\left |\sqrt{2}+i(1-\sqrt{2})\right |^{2}=(\sqrt{2})^{2}+(1-\sqrt{2})^{2}$

$=2+(1-2\sqrt{2}+2)=5-2\sqrt{2}$

Thus, the expression $|z_{1}\bar{z}_{2}+z_{2}\bar{z}_{3}+z_{3}\bar{z}_{1}|^{2}$ simplifies as follows:

$α=5$

$β=-2$

Finally, compute $α^{2}+β^{2}$:

$α^{2}+β^{2}=5^{2}+(-2)^{2}=25+4=29$

Therefore, the value of $α^{2}+β^{2}$ is 29.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text: Let $\mathrm{L}_{1}:\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y-2}{3}=\frac{z-3}{4}$ and $\mathrm{L}_{2}:\frac{x-2}{3}=\frac{y-4}{4}=\frac{z-5}{5}$ be two lines. Then which of the following points lies on the line of the shortest distance between $\mathrm{L}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{L}_{2}$ ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Points on the two lines are taken as the feet of the common perpendicular:

$P(2λ+1,3λ+2,4λ+3),Q(3μ+2,4μ+4,5μ+5)$


[IMG]

The common perpendicular is along

$\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \end{array}\right |=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$

$PQ\leftarrow =(3μ-2λ+1,4μ-3λ+2,5μ-4λ+2)$ is perpendicular to both lines:

$2(3μ-2λ+1)+3(4μ-3λ+2)+4(5μ-4λ+2)=0\Rightarrow 38μ-29λ+16=0$

$3(3μ-2λ+1)+4(4μ-3λ+2)+5(5μ-4λ+2)=0\Rightarrow 50μ-38λ+21=0$

Solving, $λ=\dfrac{1}{3}$ and $μ=-\dfrac{1}{6}$, so $P\left (\dfrac{5}{3},3,\dfrac{13}{3}\right )$, $Q\left (\dfrac{3}{2},\dfrac{10}{3},\dfrac{25}{6}\right )$ and $PQ\leftarrow =\left (-\dfrac{1}{6},\dfrac{1}{3},-\dfrac{1}{6}\right )\| (1,-2,1)$.

The line of shortest distance is

$\frac{x-\frac{5}{3}}{1}=\frac{y-3}{-2}=\frac{z-\frac{13}{3}}{1}$

For $\left (\dfrac{14}{3},-3,\dfrac{22}{3}\right )$ the three ratios are $\dfrac{14/3-5/3}{1}=3$, $\dfrac{-3-3}{-2}=3$ and $\dfrac{22/3-13/3}{1}=3$, so this point lies on the line. For (B) the $x$- and $y$-ratios are $\dfrac{1}{3}$ and $0$, for (C) $1$ and $2$, for (D) $-\dfrac{10}{3}$ and $5$, so none of these lies on it.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: Let $A=\{1,2,3,\ldots ,10\}$ and $B=\left \{\frac{m}{n}:m,n\in A,m<n \right.$ and $\gcd (m,n)=1\}$. Then $n(B)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the number of elements in set $B$, we consider pairs $\left (\frac{m}{n}\right )$ where $m,n\in A$ with $m<n$ and $\text{gcd}(m,n)=1$.

Here's the breakdown for each possible $m$:

For $m=1$:  

Possible values for $n$ are $2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10$.  

Total pairs: $9$.

For $m=2$:  

Possible values for $n$ are $3,5,7,9$ (since these have $\text{gcd}(2,n)=1$).  

Total pairs: $4$.

For $m=3$:  

Possible values for $n$ are $4,5,7,8,10$.  

Total pairs: $5$.

For $m=4$:  

Possible values for $n$ are $5,7,9$.  

Total pairs: $3$.

For $m=5$:  

Possible values for $n$ are $6,7,8,9$.  

Total pairs: $4$.

For $m=6$:  

Possible value for $n$ is $7$.  

Total pairs: $1$.

For $m=7$:  

Possible values for $n$ are $8,9,10$.  

Total pairs: $3$.

For $m=8$:  

Possible value for $n$ is $9$.  

Total pairs: $1$.

For $m=9$:  

Possible value for $n$ is $10$.  

Total pairs: $1$.

Adding all these up, the total number of elements in set $B$ is:

$9+4+5+3+4+1+3+1+1=31$

text: Let the triangle PQR be the image of the triangle with vertices $(1,3),(3,1)$ and $(2,4)$ in the line $x+2y=2$. If the centroid of $△\mathrm{PQR}$ is the point $(α,β)$, then $15(α-β)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Let ' $G$ ' be the centroid of $\Delta$ formed by $(1,3)(3,1)$ & $(2,4)$

$\mathrm{G}\cong \left (2,\frac{8}{3}\right )$

Image of G w.r.t. $x+2y-2=0$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{α-2}{1}=\dfrac{β-\frac{8}{3}}{2}=-2\dfrac{\left (2+\frac{16}{3}-2\right )}{1+4} \\ =\dfrac{-2}{5}\left (\dfrac{16}{3}\right ) \\ \Rightarrow α=\dfrac{-32}{15}+2=\dfrac{-2}{15},β=\dfrac{-32\times 2}{15}+\dfrac{8}{3}=\dfrac{-24}{15} \\ 15(α-β)=-2+24=22 \end{array}$

text: The product of all solutions of the equation $\mathrm{e}^{5(\log _{\mathrm{e}}x)^{2}+3}=x^{8},x>0$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We begin with the equation:

$e^{5(\log _{e}x)^{2}+3}=x^{8},x>0.$

Equating the exponents, we have:

$5(\log _{e}x)^{2}+3=\log _{e}x^{8}=8\log _{e}x.$

Let $t=\log _{e}x$. Substituting, the equation becomes:

$5t^{2}+3=8t.$

Rewriting this as a quadratic equation:

$5t^{2}-8t+3=0.$

Factoring the quadratic:

$5t^{2}-5t-3t+3=0,$

$(5t-3)(t-1)=0.$

Thus, the solutions for $t$ are:

$t=1$ implies $\log _{e}x=1$, giving $x=e$.

$t=\frac{3}{5}$ implies $\log _{e}x=\frac{3}{5}$, giving $x=e^{\frac{3}{5}}$.

The product of all solutions is:

$e^{1}\times e^{\frac{3}{5}}=e^{1+\frac{3}{5}}=e^{\frac{8}{5}}.$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text: From all the English alphabets, five letters are chosen and are arranged in alphabetical order. The total number of ways, in which the middle letter is ' M ', is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
First, note that we are choosing 5 distinct letters (in strictly increasing alphabetical order) such that the middle (third) letter is ‘M’. Symbolically, if we denote the chosen letters as:

$L_{1}<L_{2}<L_{3}<L_{4}<L_{5},$

we want $L_{3}=\text{M}$. The English alphabet has 26 letters, and M is the $13^{\text{th}}$.

Step 1: Letters before M

The letters before M are $\{A,B,C,\ldots ,L\}$.  

There are 12 letters here ($A$ through $L$).  

We need to pick 2 of these 12 letters to occupy $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$.  

The number of ways to choose 2 letters out of 12 is ${}^{12}\mathrm{C}_{2}$.

Step 2: Letters after M

The letters after M are $\{N,O,P,\ldots ,Z\}$.  

There are 13 letters here ($N$ through $Z$).  

We need to pick 2 of these 13 letters to occupy $L_{4}$ and $L_{5}$.  

The number of ways to choose 2 letters out of 13 is ${}^{13}\mathrm{C}_{2}$.

Step 3: Multiply the choices
Since these choices are independent (picking the two letters before M and two letters after M), the total number of ways is:

${}^{12}\mathrm{C}_{2}\qquad \times {}^{13}\mathrm{C}_{2}$

Calculate each combination:

${}^{12}\mathrm{C}_{2}=\frac{12\times 11}{2}=66,{}^{13}\mathrm{C}_{2}=\frac{13\times 12}{2}=78.$

So,

${}^{12}\mathrm{C}_{2}\times {}^{13}\mathrm{C}_{2}=66\times 78=5148.$

Answer: 5148 (Option B)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text: Let $x=x(y)$ be the solution of the differential equation $y^{2}\mathrm{d}x+\left (x-\frac{1}{y}\right )\mathrm{d}y=0$. If $x(1)=1$, then $x\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Taking $x$ as the dependent variable:

$y^{2}\frac{dx}{dy}=\frac{1}{y}-x\Rightarrow \frac{dx}{dy}+\frac{x}{y^{2}}=\frac{1}{y^{3}}$

The integrating factor is $e^{\int \frac{dy}{y2}}=e^{-1/y}$, so

$xe^{-1/y}=\int e^{-1/y}\cdot \frac{1}{y^{3}}dy+C$

Put $t=-\dfrac{1}{y}$, so $dt=\dfrac{dy}{y^{2}}$ and $\dfrac{dy}{y^{3}}=\dfrac{1}{y}\cdot \dfrac{dy}{y^{2}}=-tdt$:

$\int e^{-1/y}\frac{dy}{y^{3}}=-\int te^{t}dt=-(t-1)e^{t}=e^{-1/y}\left (\frac{1}{y}+1\right )$

Thus $xe^{-1/y}=e^{-1/y}\left (\dfrac{1}{y}+1\right )+C$, i.e. $x=\dfrac{1}{y}+1+Ce^{1/y}$.

$x(1)=1$ gives $1=2+Ce$, so $C=-e^{-1}$ and $x=\dfrac{1}{y}+1-e^{\frac{1}{y}-1}$.

$x\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=2+1-e^{2-1}=3-e$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text: A coin is tossed three times. Let $X$ denote the number of times a tail follows a head. If $μ$ and $σ^{2}$ denote the mean and variance of $X$, then the value of $64\left (μ+σ^{2}\right )$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A tail follows a head once for each consecutive pair HT in the three tosses. Of the 8 equally likely outcomes, HHT, HTH, HTT and THT contain exactly one such pair, and HHH, THH, TTH and TTT contain none (two HT pairs would need at least four tosses).

So $P(X=0)=P(X=1)=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

$μ=0\cdot \frac{1}{2}+1\cdot \frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2},σ^{2}=E(X^{2})-μ^{2}=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{4}$

$64\left (μ+σ^{2}\right )=64\times \frac{3}{4}=48$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text: Let $f(x)$ be a real differentiable function such that $f(0)=1$ and $f(x+y)=f(x)f^{'}(y)+f^{'}(x)f(y)$ for all $x,y\in 𝐑$. Then $\sum\limits _{n=1}^{100}\log _{e}f(n)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Putting $x=y=0$: $f(0)=2f(0)f^{'}(0)$, and since $f(0)=1$, $f^{'}(0)=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Putting $y=0$: $f(x)=f(x)f^{'}(0)+f^{'}(x)f(0)=\dfrac{1}{2}f(x)+f^{'}(x)$, so $f^{'}(x)=\dfrac{f(x)}{2}$.

This gives $\ln f(x)=\dfrac{x}{2}+c$, and $f(0)=1$ gives $c=0$, so $f(x)=e^{x/2}$ and $\log _{e}f(n)=\dfrac{n}{2}$.

$\sum\limits _{n=1}^{100}\log _{e}f(n)=\frac{1}{2}\sum\limits _{n=1}^{100}n=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{100\times 101}{2}=2525$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text: Two balls are selected at random one by one without replacement from a bag containing 4 white and 6 black balls. If the probability that the first selected ball is black, given that the second selected ball is also black, is $\frac{m}{n}$, where $\gcd (m,n)=1$, then $m+n$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In a bag containing 4 white and 6 black balls, two balls are selected one by one without replacement. We need to find the probability that the first ball is black, given that the second ball is black. Let’s define the events:

A: The first ball selected is black.

B: The second ball selected is black.

The probability $P(A|B)$ is given by the formula:

$P(A|B)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}$

Let's compute each part separately:

Probability of both balls being black $P(A\cap B)$:  

The chance that the first ball is black is $\frac{6}{10}$. Given that one black ball is removed, the probability that the second is also black is $\frac{5}{9}$.

$P(A\cap B)=\frac{6}{10}\times \frac{5}{9}=\frac{30}{90}=\frac{1}{3}$

Probability that the second ball is black $P(B)$:  

This can occur if either the first ball was white or black:

First ball white, second black: $\frac{4}{10}\times \frac{6}{9}$

Both balls black: $\frac{6}{10}\times \frac{5}{9}$

$P(B)=\frac{4}{10}\times \frac{6}{9}+\frac{6}{10}\times \frac{5}{9}=\frac{24}{90}+\frac{30}{90}=\frac{54}{90}=\frac{3}{5}$

Now, using these probabilities:

$P(A|B)=\frac{\frac{1}{3}}{\frac{3}{5}}=\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{5}{3}=\frac{5}{9}$

Here, $\frac{5}{9}$ is in its simplest form ($\gcd (5,9)=1$), so $m=5$ and $n=9$.

Therefore, $m+n=5+9=14$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text: Let $a_{1},a_{2},a_{3},\ldots$ be a G.P. of increasing positive terms. If $a_{1}a_{5}=28$ and $a_{2}+a_{4}=29$, then $a_{6}$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
First, let us denote the first term of the G.P. by $a_{1}=A$ and the common ratio (which is $>1$, since the G.P. is increasing) by $r$. Then the terms are:

$a_{1}=A,a_{2}=Ar,a_{3}=Ar^{2},a_{4}=Ar^{3},a_{5}=Ar^{4},a_{6}=Ar^{5},\ldots$

We are given:

$a_{1}\cdot a_{5}=28$, i.e.

$A\cdot (Ar^{4})=A^{2}r^{4}=28.(1)$

$a_{2}+a_{4}=29$, i.e.

$Ar+Ar^{3}=A(r+r^{3})=29.(2)$

We want to find $a_{6}=Ar^{5}$.

1. Solve for $r$
From $\text{(1)}$:  

$A^{2}r^{4}=28⟹A^{2}=\frac{28}{r^{4}}.$

From $\text{(2)}$:  

$A\left (r+r^{3}\right )=29⟹A=\frac{29}{r+r^{3}}.$

Plug $A$ from $\text{(2)}$ into $\text{(1)}$.  After some algebra (or by a systematic approach), one finds that  

$r^{2}=28⟹r=\sqrt{28}=2\sqrt{7}$

(since $r>1$, we take the positive root).

2. Solve for $A$
From (2), using $r=2\sqrt{7}$:

$r+r^{3}=2\sqrt{7}+(2\sqrt{7})^{3}=2\sqrt{7}+56\sqrt{7}=58\sqrt{7}.$

Hence,

$A=\frac{29}{58\sqrt{7}}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{7}}.$

3. Find $a_{6}$
$a_{6}=Ar^{5}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{7}}\times (2\sqrt{7})^{5}.$

Compute $(2\sqrt{7})^{5}$. First, $(2\sqrt{7})^{2}=28$; thus

$(2\sqrt{7})^{5}=(2\sqrt{7})^{4}\cdot (2\sqrt{7})=784\times (2\sqrt{7})=1568\sqrt{7}.$

Therefore,

$a_{6}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{7}}\cdot 1568\sqrt{7}=\frac{1568}{2}(\text{since}\sqrt{7}\text{cancels})=784.$

Answer: $a_{6}=784$.
Hence, the correct option is Option B.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text: Let for $f(x)=7\tan ^{8}x+7\tan ^{6}x-3\tan ^{4}x-3\tan ^{2}x,\mathrm{I}_{1}=\int\limits _{0}^{π/4}f(x)\mathrm{d}x$ and $\mathrm{I}_{2}=\int\limits _{0}^{π/4}xf(x)\mathrm{d}x$. Then $7\mathrm{I}_{1}+12\mathrm{I}_{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{ll} f(x) & =7\tan ^{8}x+7\tan ^{6}x-3\tan ^{4}x-3\tan ^{2}x \\ \qquad =7\tan ^{6}x\left (1+\tan ^{2}x\right )-3\tan ^{2}x\left (1+\tan ^{2}x\right ) \\ \qquad =\left (7\tan ^{6}x-3\tan ^{2}x\right )\left (1+\tan ^{2}x\right ) \\ \qquad =\left (7\tan ^{6}x-3\tan ^{2}x\right )\sec ^{2}x \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll} I_{1}= & \int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}f(x)dx=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}\left (7\tan ^{6}x-3\tan ^{2}x\right )\sec ^{2}xdx \\ \qquad =\left (\dfrac{7\tan ^{7}x}{7}-\dfrac{3\tan ^{3}x}{3}\right )\left |_{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}=1-1=0 \end{array} \right.$

$\begin{array}{ll} I_{2}= & \int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}xf(x)dx=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}x\left (7\tan ^{6}x-3\tan ^{2}x\right )\sec ^{2}xdx \\ \qquad =x\left (\tan ^{7}x-\tan ^{3}x\right )\left |_{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}-\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}1\cdot \left (\tan ^{7}x-\tan ^{3}x\right )dx \\ \qquad =0-\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}\tan ^{3}x\left (\tan ^{2}x-1\right )\left (\tan ^{2}x+1\right )dx \end{array} \right.$

$\begin{array}{l} =\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{4}}\left (\tan ^{3}x-\tan ^{5}x\right )\sec ^{2}xdx=\dfrac{\tan ^{4}x}{4}-\dfrac{\tan ^{6}x}{6}\left |_{0}^{\frac{π}{4}} \\ =\dfrac{1}{12} \end{array} \right.$

Hence $7I_{1}+12I_{2}=1$

text: The number of non-empty equivalence relations on the set $\{1,2,3\}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An equivalence relation on a finite set is uniquely determined by its partition into equivalence classes. Hence, counting the number of equivalence relations on a set is equivalent to counting the number of ways to partition that set.

Step: Counting partitions of $\{1,2,3\}$
We want all possible ways to split the set $\{1,2,3\}$ into nonempty subsets (its “blocks”).

3 blocks (each element in its own block)  

$\{\{1\},\{2\},\{3\}\}.$

2 blocks  

$\{\{1,2\},\{3\}\}$  

$\{\{1,3\},\{2\}\}$  

$\{\{2,3\},\{1\}\}$

1 block (all elements together)  

$\{\{1,2,3\}\}.$

Counting these, there are a total of 5 distinct partitions, and thus 5 equivalence relations on the set $\{1,2,3\}$. 

All equivalence relations are automatically nonempty (they include at least $(1,1),(2,2),(3,3)$ because they are reflexive), so the answer to “the number of nonempty equivalence relations” is also 5.

Answer: Option C (5)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text: Let the parabola $y=x^{2}+\mathrm{p}x-3$, meet the coordinate axes at the points $\mathrm{P},\mathrm{Q}$ and R . If the circle C with centre at $(-1,-1)$ passes through the points $P,Q$ and $R$, then the area of $△PQR$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The given parabola is $y=x^{2}+px-3$.

Intersection with the y-axis:

At $x=0$, we find $y=-3$.

Thus, the parabola intersects the y-axis at the point $(0,-3)$.

Circle Equation:

We are given the circle has its center at $(-1,-1)$ and it passes through the points where the parabola intersects the axes. The radius can be found using the distance from the center to any given point the circle passes through. Using $(0,-3)$:

$\text{Radius}=\sqrt{(0+1)^{2}+(-3+1)^{2}}=\sqrt{1^{2}+(-2)^{2}}=\sqrt{5}$

Therefore, the equation of the circle is:

$(x+1)^{2}+(y+1)^{2}=5$

This simplifies to:

$x^{2}+2x+1+y^{2}+2y+1=5$

$x^{2}+y^{2}+2x+2y+2=5$

$x^{2}+y^{2}+2x+2y-3=0$

Intersection with the x-axis:

When $y=0$, solving the quadratic $x^{2}+2x-3=0$ gives:

$(x+3)(x-1)=0$

So, $x=-3$ or $x=1$.

Thus, the intersection points on the x-axis are $(-3,0)$ and $(1,0)$.

Vertices of Triangle $△PQR$:

The vertices of the triangle formed are $P=(0,-3)$, $Q=(-3,0)$, and $R=(1,0)$.

Area of $△PQR$:

Use the determinant formula to find the area of the triangle:

$\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}\left |\begin{array}{lll} 0 & -3 & 1 \\ -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right |$

Calculate the determinant:

$=\frac{1}{2}((0)(0)(1)+(-3)(1)(1)+(1)(-3)(1)-(1)(0)(1)-(-3)(1)(0)-(0)(-3)(1))$

Simplify:

$=\frac{1}{2}(0-3+3+0)=\frac{1}{2}(12)=6$

Thus, the area of $△PQR$ is 6.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift

text: Using the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, the sum of the maximum and the minimum values of $16\left (\left (\sec ^{-1}x\right )^{2}+\left (\mathrm{cosec}^{-1}x\right )^{2}\right )$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $f(x)=16\left [\left (\sec ^{-1}x\right )^{2}+\left (\mathrm{cosec}^{-1}x\right )^{2}\right ]$.

We can express $f(x)$ as:

$f(x)=16\left [\left (\sec ^{-1}x+\mathrm{cosec}^{-1}x\right )^{2}-2\left (\sec ^{-1}x\right )\left (\frac{π}{2}-\sec ^{-1}x\right )\right ]$

This simplifies to:

$f(x)=16\left [\frac{π^{2}}{4}-π\sec ^{-1}x+2\left (\sec ^{-1}x\right )^{2}\right ],\text{where}\sec ^{-1}x\in [0,π]-\left \{\frac{π}{2}\right \}$

Further simplification gives:

$f(x)=16\left [2\left (\sec ^{-1}x-\frac{π}{4}\right )^{2}+\frac{π^{2}}{4}-\frac{π^{2}}{8}\right ]$

For the maximum value when $\sec ^{-1}x=π$:

$\max =16\left [2π^{2}-π^{2}+\frac{π^{2}}{4}\right ]=20π^{2}$

For the minimum value when $\sec ^{-1}x=\frac{π}{4}$:

$\min =16\left [\frac{2\times π^{2}}{16}-\frac{π^{2}}{4}+\frac{π^{2}}{4}\right ]=2π^{2}$

Therefore, the sum of the maximum and minimum values is:

$\text{Sum}=22π^{2}$

text: Let $f:𝐑\to 𝐑$ be a twice differentiable function such that $f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)$ for all $x,y\in 𝐑$. If $f^{'}(0)=4\mathrm{a}$ and $f$ satisfies $f^{''}(x)-3\mathrm{a}f^{'}(x)-f(x)=0,\mathrm{a}>0$, then the area of the region $\mathrm{R}=\{(x,y)|0\leq y\leq f(ax),0\leq x\leq 2\}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y})=\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{y}) \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{e}^{λ\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{f}^{'}(0)=4\mathrm{a} \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}^{'}(\mathrm{x})=λ\mathrm{e}^{λ\mathrm{x}}\Rightarrow λ=4\mathrm{a} \end{array}$

So, $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{e}^{4\mathrm{ax}}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{f}^{''}(\mathrm{x})-3\mathrm{af}^{'}(\mathrm{x})-\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=0 \\ \Rightarrow λ^{2}-3\mathrm{a}λ-1=0 \\ \Rightarrow 16\mathrm{a}^{2}-12\mathrm{a}^{2}-1=0\Rightarrow 4\mathrm{a}^{2}=1\Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=\dfrac{1}{2} \end{array}$


[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{e}^{2\mathrm{x}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{ax})=\mathrm{f}\left (\dfrac{\mathrm{x}}{2}\right )=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}} \\ \text{Area}=\int\limits _{0}^{2}\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{dx}=\mathrm{e}^{2}-1 \end{array}$

text: Let $⃗{c}$ be the projection vector of $⃗{b}=λ\hat{i}+4\hat{k},λ>0$, on the vector $⃗{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$. If $|⃗{a}+⃗{c}|=7$, then the area of the parallelogram formed by the vectors $⃗{b}$ and $⃗{c}$ is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the projection vector $⃗{c}$ of $⃗{b}=λ\hat{i}+4\hat{k}$ (where $λ>0$) onto vector $⃗{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$, we use the formula for the projection of a vector:

$⃗{c}=\left (\frac{⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{a}}{|⃗{a}|^{2}}\right )⃗{a}$

Calculate the dot product $⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{a}$:

$⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{a}=(λ\hat{i}+4\hat{k})\cdot (\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})=λ\cdot 1+4\cdot 2=λ+8$

Calculate the magnitude of $⃗{a}$:

$|⃗{a}|=\sqrt{1^{2}+2^{2}+2^{2}}=\sqrt{9}=3$

Now substitute to find $⃗{c}$:

$⃗{c}=\left (\frac{λ+8}{9}\right )(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})$

We know that the magnitude $|⃗{a}+⃗{c}|=7$. Thus, substituting $⃗{c}$ in this equation, we resolve it to find $λ$:

$⃗{a}+⃗{c}=\left (1+\frac{λ+8}{9}\right )⃗{a}\Rightarrow |⃗{a}+⃗{c}|=3\cdot \frac{λ+17}{9}=\frac{λ+17}{3}=7\Rightarrow λ=4$

This indicates that $λ$ has a value of 4.

Next, calculating the area of the parallelogram formed by vectors $⃗{b}$ and $⃗{c}$ involves finding the cross product $|⃗{b}\times ⃗{c}|$:

$⃗{b}=4\hat{i}+4\hat{k},⃗{c}=\left (\frac{12}{9}\right )(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})=\left (\frac{4}{3}\right )\hat{i}+\left (\frac{8}{3}\right )\hat{j}+\left (\frac{8}{3}\right )\hat{k}$

The cross product is:

$⃗{b}\times ⃗{c}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{ı} & \hat{ȷ} & \hat{k} \\ 4 & 0 & 4 \\ \frac{4}{3} & \frac{8}{3} & \frac{8}{3} \end{array}\right |$

Solving the determinant:

$⃗{b}\times ⃗{c}=\left (\left (0\times \frac{8}{3}-4\times \frac{8}{3}\right )\hat{i}-\left (4\times \frac{8}{3}-4\times \frac{4}{3}\right )\hat{j}+\left (4\times \frac{8}{3}-0\times \frac{4}{3}\right )\hat{k}\right )$

$=\left (-\frac{32}{3}\hat{i}-\frac{16}{3}\hat{j}+\frac{32}{3}\hat{k}\right )$

Then, the magnitude is calculated as:

$|⃗{b}\times ⃗{c}|=\sqrt{\left (-\frac{32}{3}\right )^{2}+\left (-\frac{16}{3}\right )^{2}+\left (\frac{32}{3}\right )^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1024+256+1024}{9}}=\sqrt{\frac{2304}{9}}$

$=\frac{48}{3}=16$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram formed by $⃗{b}$ and $⃗{c}$ is 16.

text: Let $\mathrm{L}_{1}:\frac{x-1}{3}=\frac{y-1}{-1}=\frac{z+1}{0}$ and $\mathrm{L}_{2}:\frac{x-2}{2}=\frac{y}{0}=\frac{z+4}{α},α\in 𝐑$, be two lines, which intersect at the point $B$. If $P$ is the foot of perpendicular from the point $A(1,1,-1)$ on $L_{2}$, then the value of $26α(\mathrm{PB})^{2}$ is $_________$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Explanation

To find the value of $26α(\mathrm{PB})^{2}$, we proceed as follows:

Intersection Point $B$ of $\mathrm{L}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{L}_{2}$

We are given the equations of the lines:

$\mathrm{L}_{1}:\frac{x-1}{3}=\frac{y-1}{-1}=\frac{z+1}{0}$

$\mathrm{L}_{2}:\frac{x-2}{2}=\frac{y}{0}=\frac{z+4}{α}$

For $\mathrm{L}_{1}$, $z+1=0$, which implies $z=-1$.

For $\mathrm{L}_{2}$, since $y=0$, the direction ratios can be matched using the parameter $μ$:

$\begin{array}{l} x=3λ+1,y=-λ+1,z=-1, \\ x=2μ+2,y=0,z=αμ-4. \end{array}$

Setting the coordinates equal for intersection:

$\begin{array}{l} 3λ+1=2μ+2, \\ -λ+1=0, \\ -1=αμ-4. \end{array}$

From $-λ+1=0$, we find $λ=1$.

Substituting $λ=1$ into  $3λ+1=2μ+2$ gives:

$3(1)+1=2μ+2⟹μ=1.$

Also, substituting $μ=1$ into $-1=αμ-4$ gives:

$-1=α(1)-4⟹α=3.$

So, the intersection point $B$ is:

$B(4,0,-1).$

Foot of Perpendicular from $A$ to $\mathrm{L}_{2}$

The point $P$ on $\mathrm{L}_{2}$ is given by:

$P(2δ+2,0,3δ-4).$

For vector $AP\leftarrow =(2δ+1,-1,3δ-3)$, since $AP$ is perpendicular to $\mathrm{L}_{2}$, the dot product should be zero:

$\begin{array}{ll} (2δ+1)\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 0+(3δ-3)\cdot 3 & =0. \end{array}$

Simplifying gives:

$4δ+2+9δ-9=0⟹13δ=7⟹δ=\frac{7}{13}.$

So, the coordinates of point $P$ are:

$P\left (\frac{40}{13},0,\frac{-31}{13}\right ).$

Distance $\mathrm{PB}$ and Calculation

The vector $PB\leftarrow$ is:

$PB\leftarrow =\left (4-\frac{40}{13},0-0,-1-\left (\frac{-31}{13}\right )\right ).$

Calculating the components:

$PB\leftarrow =\left (\frac{12}{13},0,\frac{18}{13}\right ).$

The square of the distance $(PB)^{2}$ is:

$\left (\frac{12}{13}\right )^{2}+(0)^{2}+\left (\frac{18}{13}\right )^{2}=\frac{144}{169}+\frac{324}{169}=\frac{468}{169}.$

Thus, $26α(PB)^{2}$ is:

$26\times 3\times \frac{468}{169}=216.$ 

So, the final value is 216.

text: Let $A$ be a square matrix of order 3 such that $\det (A)=-2$ and $\det (3\mathrm{adj}(-6\mathrm{adj}(3A)))=2^{m+n}\cdot 3^{mn},m>n$. Then $4m+2n$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \text{As}A\mathrm{adj}A=|A|I,\det (λA)=λ^{n}\det A \\  \\ \det (3\mathrm{adj}(-6\mathrm{adj}(3A)))=3^{3}\det (\mathrm{adj}(-6\mathrm{adj}(3A))) \\  \\ =3^{3}|-6\mathrm{adj}(3A)|^{2} \\  \\ =3^{3}(-6)^{6}|3A|^{4} \\  \\ =3^{9}2^{6}\cdot 3^{12}\cdot (-2)^{4} \\  \\ =3^{21}\cdot 2^{10} \end{array}$

Now comparing with given condition

$\begin{array}{l} 2^{m+n}3^{mn}=2^{10}\cdot 3^{21} \\  \\ m+n=10,mn=21 \\  \\ \Rightarrow m=7,n=3(m>n) \\  \\ \therefore 4m+2n=28+6=34 \end{array}$
